Response and design matrices from a model formula

Source: R/animal_design.R
animal_design.Rd

Builds the Y and X arguments of lmm_animal, lm_phen_cov and lmm_animal_gibbs from a formula and a data frame, so a model written the usual way (y ~ sex + age, or cbind(x, y, z) ~ sex + age) can be fitted without building the matrices by hand.

Usage

animal_design(
  formula,
  data,
  na.action = stats::na.omit,
  pedigree = NULL,
  genotypes = NULL,
  Gamma = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula. The left-hand side is a single response or cbind() of several traits; the right-hand side lists the fixed effects.

data

Data frame holding the variables in formula. When pedigree or genotypes are used, its row names must be the individual IDs (rownames(data) <- data$id); an error says so when they were left to R.

na.action

How to handle rows with missing predictors, passed to model.frame; the default drops them, since a row with an unknown fixed effect cannot be placed in the design. Missing values in the response are kept: a trait that was not measured on an individual is information the model can use, and lmm_animal() integrates it out.

pedigree

Optional pedigree, used to compute the additive relationship matrix A with makeA. A data frame whose first three columns are the individual, its sire and its dam, with 0, NA or "" for unknown parents. The pedigree may contain ancestors that are not in data.

genotypes

Optional genotype matrix, used to compute a genomic relationship matrix (see genomic_relationship): individuals in rows, with their IDs as row names, and biallelic markers in columns, coded 0, 1, 2.

Gamma

Optional relationship matrix among pedigree founders, or among founder groups when groups is given; passed to makeA. Only used with pedigree.

groups

Optional founder-to-group assignment passed to makeA; only used with pedigree and Gamma.

...

Further arguments passed to genomic_relationship, such as p, maf or blend.

Value

A list with

Y

response matrix, one column per trait, named after the response(s) in the formula;

X

fixed-effects design matrix, with columns named after the terms in the formula;

A

relationship matrix, present only when pedigree or genotypes is given, restricted to the individuals in Y and in the same row and column order.

Rows are in the order of data. attr(, "individuals") holds the row names of data for the rows kept, so naming the rows with the individual IDs lets a relationship matrix A be matched to Y: lmm_animal puts a named A in the row order of Y and errors if the names disagree.

Details

Random-effect terms such as (1 | animal) are ignored, so formulas written for lme4 can be reused unchanged: relatedness is supplied through A, which is passed to the model directly.

The result satisfies what the model functions expect: Y is numeric and X has full column rank. Factor predictors are dummy coded and the intercept is kept unless the formula removes it, so the columns of X match the beta draws reported by a fit. Removing the intercept is only allowed when the remaining columns still sum to a constant, as the 0/1 indicators of a factor do, because the models centre the responses and report their mean back through the design; a formula such as y ~ 0 + x is an error.

When pedigree or genotypes is given, A is computed for all individuals in the pedigree or genotype matrix and then subset to the rows of Y, so ancestors without records and individuals with missing phenotypes are handled: every row of Y must appear in the pedigree or in the row names of the genotype matrix. With pedigree, Gamma and groups allow related founders or metafounder groups; see makeA.

If the response has three or more traits and its first principal component explains at least 80% of the variance, a warning suggests fitting size and shape scores instead (see size_shape); pc1_variance_share reports that share. If the diagnostic cannot be computed, a warning explains why; the design is still returned.

See also

lmm_animal, makeA, genomic_relationship, rename_beta

Examples

dat <- data.frame(trait = rnorm(6), x = rnorm(6),
                  sex = rep(c(0, 1), each = 3), id = 1:6)
rownames(dat) <- dat$id
design <- animal_design(trait ~ sex + x, dat)
design$Y
#>          trait
#> 1 -1.400043517
#> 2  0.255317055
#> 3 -2.437263611
#> 4 -0.005571287
#> 5  0.621552721
#> 6  1.148411606
design$X
#>   (Intercept) sex          x
#> 1           1   0 -1.8218177
#> 2           1   0 -0.2473253
#> 3           1   0 -0.2441996
#> 4           1   1 -0.2827054
#> 5           1   1 -0.5536994
#> 6           1   1  0.6289820
#> attr(,"assign")
#> [1] 0 1 2

# formulas written for lme4 work as they are; the random term is ignored
animal_design(trait ~ sex + (1 | id), dat)
#> $Y
#>          trait
#> 1 -1.400043517
#> 2  0.255317055
#> 3 -2.437263611
#> 4 -0.005571287
#> 5  0.621552721
#> 6  1.148411606
#> 
#> $X
#>   (Intercept) sex
#> 1           1   0
#> 2           1   0
#> 3           1   0
#> 4           1   1
#> 5           1   1
#> 6           1   1
#> attr(,"assign")
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> attr(,"individuals")
#> [1] "1" "2" "3" "4" "5" "6"

# relatedness from a pedigree (first three columns: id, sire, dam)
ped <- data.frame(id = 1:6, sire = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 4, 4),
                  dam = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 5))
design <- animal_design(trait ~ sex, dat, pedigree = ped)
round(design$A, 2)
#>     1   2    3    4    5    6
#> 1 1.0 0.0 0.50 0.50 0.50 0.50
#> 2 0.0 1.0 0.50 0.50 0.50 0.50
#> 3 0.5 0.5 1.00 0.50 0.75 0.62
#> 4 0.5 0.5 0.50 1.00 0.75 0.88
#> 5 0.5 0.5 0.75 0.75 1.25 1.00
#> 6 0.5 0.5 0.62 0.88 1.00 1.38

# related founders: pass their relationship matrix as Gamma
Gamma <- matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1), 2,
                dimnames = list(c("1", "2"), c("1", "2")))
design <- animal_design(trait ~ sex, dat, pedigree = ped, Gamma = Gamma)
round(design$A, 2)
#>      1    2    3    4    5    6
#> 1 1.00 0.50 0.75 0.75 0.75 0.75
#> 2 0.50 1.00 0.75 0.75 0.75 0.75
#> 3 0.75 0.75 1.25 0.75 1.00 0.88
#> 4 0.75 0.75 0.75 1.25 1.00 1.12
#> 5 0.75 0.75 1.00 1.00 1.38 1.19
#> 6 0.75 0.75 0.88 1.12 1.19 1.50

# relatedness from genotypes (individuals in rows, markers in columns)
M <- matrix(rbinom(6 * 40, 2, 0.3), 6,
            dimnames = list(as.character(1:6), NULL))
design <- animal_design(trait ~ sex, dat, genotypes = M, blend = 0.01)
dim(design$A)
#> [1] 6 6
